title: Validate the selected BigQuery credential in nested and flat payloads
answers: Why can a BigQuery source save without credentials?
How does BigQuery validate a bare auth_type string?
Can credentials from the other authentication option satisfy validation?
body:
Symptom: A BigQuery source saves without a usable credential when the authentication choice arrives as a bare string.
Root cause: products/warehouse_sources/backend/temporal/data_imports/sources/bigquery/source.py:BigQuerySource.validate_config previously returned before checking credentials for a string auth_type.
Fix pattern: Normalize the selection and credential container before validation: string auth_type uses top-level job_inputs; dictionary auth_type uses its selection and nested fields. Validate the credential required by that selection.
Constraints: Form credential fields are optional because unselected options must not block saving, so the source-level check must remain. Credentials belonging to the unselected option must not satisfy the selected option; cover both shapes in products/warehouse_sources/backend/temporal/data_imports/sources/bigquery/tests/test_source.py:test_bigquery_validate_config_requires_the_credential_for_the_selected_auth_type and test_bigquery_validate_config_reads_a_bare_selection_from_the_flat_payload.
applies: Changes to BigQuery authentication selection parsing or credential validation for nested and flat configuration payloads.
